questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a kingdom in Whittaker's five kingdom classification?
questions.explanation: The five kingdoms are Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia; protozoans are placed within Protista.

questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A plant bending towards light and an animal withdrawing from a hot object both show that living organisms
options: respond to stimuli from the environment
questions.explanation: Sensing and responding to environmental stimuli is a property of all living organisms.

questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A group of related orders is placed in a
questions.explanation: Related orders form a class, and related classes form a phylum or division.

questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A book that gives the description of the plants found in a particular area is called a
questions.explanation: A flora records the plants of an area with their names and descriptions.

questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Which feature is shown by a living cell but NOT by a growing crystal of salt?
questions.explanation: A crystal increases in size by accumulation but has no metabolic reactions.

questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: The lion (Panthera leo) and the domestic cat (Felis domestica) share which lowest taxonomic category?
questions.explanation: Both belong to family Felidae, but they are placed in different genera.

questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Name two taxonomic aids and state one use of each.
questions.answer: A herbarium stores dried pressed plant specimens for identification; a museum keeps preserved animal specimens for study; a botanical garden or zoo shows living organisms; a key helps identify organisms.
questions.explanation: Taxonomic aids help in identification and classification.

questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Why is metabolism considered the most dependable defining feature of life?
questions.answer: All living organisms, including sterile ones, carry out chemical reactions inside the body, whereas non-living objects do not. Features like growth or reproduction may be absent in some living beings, but metabolism never is.
keyPoints: Growth or reproduction can be absent in some living organisms
questions.explanation: Metabolism is the sum of all chemical reactions in the body.

questions.q: Which of the following is a brown alga?
questions.explanation: Laminaria, Fucus and Sargassum are brown algae.

questions.q: Plants whose seeds are enclosed within fruits are
questions.explanation: Angiosperms bear flowers, and the ovary develops into the fruit enclosing the seeds.

questions.q: Angiosperms with seeds having a single cotyledon are called
questions.explanation: Monocots such as wheat and maize have one cotyledon.

questions.q: The main plant body of a moss or liverwort is the
questions.explanation: The dominant phase of bryophytes is the haploid gametophyte.

questions.q: In a moss, meiosis occurs in the
questions.explanation: Spore mother cells in the capsule of the sporophyte divide meiotically to form haploid spores.

questions.q: In seed plants the female gametophyte is retained within the
questions.explanation: The megaspore develops into the female gametophyte inside the ovule.

questions.q: Write three differences between monocotyledons and dicotyledons.
questions.answer: Monocots have one cotyledon, parallel leaf venation and fibrous roots; dicots have two cotyledons, reticulate venation and a tap root system.
questions.explanation: Floral parts are in threes in monocots and fours or fives in dicots.

questions.q: Why is Selaginella considered a step towards the seed habit?
questions.answer: Selaginella is heterosporous, producing megaspores and microspores; the female gametophyte develops within the megaspore, which is retained on the parent sporophyte, and the zygote develops into the young embryo there, as in seed plants.
keyPoints: Female gametophyte retained on the parent
Embryo develops in the retained structure
questions.explanation: These features anticipate the seed habit.

questions.q: Which of the following is a sponge?
questions.explanation: Sycon is a sponge in phylum Porifera.

questions.q: A frog belongs to class
questions.explanation: Frogs and toads belong to Amphibia.

questions.q: Octopus and Pila belong to phylum
questions.explanation: Soft-bodied animals with a mantle and a muscular foot are molluscs.

questions.q: An adult insect has how many pairs of legs?
questions.explanation: Insects have three pairs of jointed legs on the thorax.

questions.q: Animals in which the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life, such as Branchiostoma, belong to
questions.explanation: In cephalochordates the notochord persists in the adult.

questions.q: In which group is the notochord present only in the tail of the larva?
questions.explanation: In urochordates such as Ascidia the notochord is limited to the larval tail.

questions.q: State any two characteristics of class Reptilia.
questions.answer: Reptiles have a dry scaly skin without glands, lay shelled eggs on land, mostly have a three-chambered heart (crocodiles have four) and are cold-blooded.
questions.explanation: Lizards, snakes and turtles are reptiles.

questions.q: The adult starfish is radially symmetrical but its larva is bilaterally symmetrical. What does this suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that echinoderms evolved from bilaterally symmetrical ancestors and became radial secondarily as adults, adapted to a slow-moving or sessile life.
questions.explanation: Symmetry may change during development.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The region of the stem where a leaf arises is called the
questions.explanation: Leaves are borne at nodes, and the stretch between nodes is an internode.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Thin-walled living cells that store food and carry out photosynthesis when they contain chloroplasts form
questions.explanation: Parenchyma is the commonest simple tissue and is involved in storage and photosynthesis.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The thorns of Bougainvillea and Citrus are modifications of
questions.explanation: Thorns arise from axillary buds, so they are modified stems.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: A typical anther is
questions.explanation: A typical anther has two lobes with two pollen sacs in each.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Sapwood of a tree trunk is
options: the outer, lighter region of secondary xylem that conducts water
questions.explanation: Sapwood is the younger, functional secondary xylem near the periphery.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Hairs (trichomes) on the stem epidermis often help the plant by
questions.explanation: Trichomes reduce transpiration and may protect against herbivores.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Give one example each of a root modified for storage, support and respiration.
questions.answer: Storage: carrot or radish (also sweet potato, turnip); support: prop roots of banyan or stilt roots of maize; respiration: pneumatophores of Rhizophora.
questions.explanation: Roots show many modifications.

questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Describe how secondary growth begins in a dicot stem.
questions.answer: The cambium between xylem and phloem in each bundle (fascicular) is joined by cambium formed from cells of medullary rays (interfascicular), forming a cambial ring. It cuts off secondary xylem inwards and secondary phloem outwards.
keyPoints: Fascicular and interfascicular cambium form a ring
questions.explanation: Secondary xylem is produced in larger amount.

questions.q: Blood is a type of
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue.

questions.q: The body of a frog is divided into
questions.explanation: A frog has no neck.

questions.q: The thorax of a cockroach consists of how many segments?
questions.explanation: Prothorax, mesothorax and metathorax.

questions.q: The main nitrogenous waste of a cockroach is
questions.explanation: Cockroaches are uricotelic.

questions.q: A male frog can be distinguished from a female by the presence of
options: vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb
questions.explanation: These are the male sexual characteristics of Rana tigrina.

questions.q: Fertilisation in frogs is
questions.explanation: Eggs and sperms are released in water and fuse there.

questions.q: Differentiate between simple and compound epithelium.
questions.answer: Simple epithelium has a single layer of cells resting on the basement membrane and functions in secretion, absorption and diffusion; compound epithelium has two or more layers and mainly protects, as in the skin.
questions.explanation: Simple epithelium is of squamous, cuboidal and columnar types.

questions.q: What is meant by the portal system in the frog? Name two portal systems.
questions.answer: A portal system is one in which a vein carries blood from one organ to the capillaries of another organ before it goes to the heart. The frog has the hepatic portal system (intestine to liver) and the renal portal system (hind limbs to kidneys).
keyPoints: Vein takes blood to another capillary network
questions.explanation: The frog also shows a closed circulation.

questions.q: The cell theory was formulated by
questions.explanation: Schleiden and Schwann proposed that all living things are composed of cells.

questions.q: Among the following, the smallest known cells are those of
questions.explanation: Mycoplasmas, about 0.3 micrometre, are the smallest cells.

questions.q: The small bristle-like fibres on the bacterial cell surface that help in attachment to rocks or host tissues are
questions.explanation: Fimbriae help bacteria attach to surfaces.

questions.q: The number of membranes covering a chloroplast is
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts and mitochondria are double-membrane organelles.

questions.q: Insect flight muscle cells contain a very large number of mitochondria because they
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are abundant in cells with a high energy demand.

questions.q: Cytoplasmic bridges that pass through the cell walls and connect neighbouring plant cells are
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata connect the cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells.

questions.q: State any three functions of the Golgi apparatus.
questions.answer: It packages materials to be delivered to the intracellular targets or secreted, modifies proteins and lipids (for example glycosylation), forms glycoproteins and glycolipids, and forms lysosomes.
questions.explanation: The Golgi is the 'post office' of the cell.

questions.q: A cell that makes large quantities of protein has a very prominent nucleolus. Explain.
questions.answer: The nucleolus is the site of rRNA synthesis and ribosome assembly, so a cell making much protein needs many ribosomes and has an enlarged, active nucleolus.
questions.explanation: Ribosomes carry out protein synthesis.

questions.q: The disaccharide found in milk is
questions.explanation: Lactose is made of glucose and galactose.

questions.q: Fatty acids that have no double bonds between carbon atoms are
questions.explanation: Saturated fatty acids, like palmitic acid, have only single bonds.

questions.q: Which of the following is a monosaccharide?
questions.explanation: Fructose is a simple sugar; sucrose and lactose are disaccharides and starch is a polysaccharide.

questions.q: A nitrogenous base found in RNA but not in DNA is
questions.explanation: RNA has uracil in place of thymine.

questions.q: When all the active sites of an enzyme are occupied by substrate, increasing the substrate concentration further will
options: cause no further increase in reaction rate
questions.explanation: The rate has reached Vmax, so extra substrate has no effect.

questions.q: In the phospholipid bilayer of a membrane, the hydrophobic tails
options: face the watery surfaces on both sides
face each other, towards the interior
questions.explanation: The polar heads face the aqueous surroundings, and the non-polar tails are inside.

questions.q: Write three differences between DNA and RNA.
questions.answer: DNA has deoxyribose sugar, thymine as a base and is usually double-stranded; RNA has ribose sugar, uracil in place of thymine and is usually single-stranded.
questions.explanation: Both are nucleic acids made of nucleotides.

questions.q: What is denaturation of a protein? Why does boiling an egg cause it?
questions.answer: Denaturation is the loss of the secondary, tertiary or quaternary structure of a protein, usually by heat or extreme pH, without breaking peptide bonds. Heat unfolds the egg white proteins, so they change shape irreversibly and the egg turns solid.
questions.explanation: Denatured proteins lose their biological activity.

questions.q: Chromosomes first become visible as condensed structures in
questions.explanation: Chromatin condenses into chromosomes during prophase.

questions.q: Meiosis takes place during the formation of
questions.explanation: In animals meiosis occurs in germ cells to form gametes; in plants it forms spores.

questions.q: Mitosis of a diploid cell produces
options: two cells with half the DNA
questions.explanation: Mitosis is equational and gives identical daughter cells.

questions.q: Meiosis II is similar to
questions.explanation: In meiosis II the sister chromatids separate, as in mitosis.

questions.q: A diploid cell has 6 chromosomes (2n = 6). How many chromosomes are present in the cell at anaphase II of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Each of the two cells has 3 chromosomes with 2 chromatids; at anaphase II the chromatids separate, giving 6 chromosomes in the cell.

questions.q: The liquid endosperm of coconut is multinucleate because
questions.explanation: Free nuclear divisions occur without division of the cytoplasm, forming a syncytium.

questions.q: Name the five stages of meiotic prophase I in sequence.
questions.answer: Leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene and diakinesis.
questions.explanation: Synapsis is in zygotene and crossing over in pachytene.

questions.q: Cells of the adult heart and nerve tissue remain in G0. What does this mean and what is its consequence?
questions.answer: G0 is a quiescent stage in which cells leave the cell cycle and do not divide. Such cells remain metabolically active but cannot replace themselves when damaged, so damage to heart or nerve cells is not easily repaired.
keyPoints: Cells exit the cycle, no division
questions.explanation: Some G0 cells can re-enter the cycle in response to signals.

questions.q: Which gas is taken in by green plants during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses CO2 and water.

questions.q: Julius von Sachs showed that the green parts of plants make glucose, which is stored as
questions.explanation: Sachs found that starch is produced in the chloroplasts of illuminated leaves.

questions.q: The number of carbon atoms in RuBP, the primary CO2 acceptor of the Calvin cycle, is
questions.explanation: RuBP is a five-carbon ketose sugar, ribulose 1,5-bisphosphate.

questions.q: During the light reaction, protons accumulate in the
questions.explanation: Water splitting and the transfer of electrons release protons into the lumen, making it acidic.

questions.q: Each photosystem consists of a reaction centre and
questions.explanation: Light-harvesting pigments pass energy to the reaction centre chlorophyll a.

questions.q: At the light compensation point of a plant,
options: the rate of photosynthesis equals the rate of respiration
questions.explanation: Net gas exchange is nil at the compensation point.

questions.q: Differentiate between the C3 and C4 pathways with reference to the first product and the site of the Calvin cycle.
questions.answer: In the C3 pathway the first stable product is the three-carbon 3-PGA, and the Calvin cycle occurs in mesophyll cells. In the C4 pathway the first product is the four-carbon OAA formed in mesophyll, and the Calvin cycle occurs in bundle sheath cells.
keyPoints: Calvin cycle in mesophyll or bundle sheath
questions.explanation: C4 plants have Kranz anatomy.

questions.q: What is the compensation point? Why can a plant not grow if it stays at this point?
questions.answer: It is the light intensity at which the rate of photosynthesis equals the rate of respiration, so there is no net gain of food. Without a surplus of sugar, the plant cannot make new tissue for growth.
questions.explanation: Shade plants have lower compensation points.

questions.q: The process in which food such as glucose is oxidised to release energy in cells is
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration releases energy stored in food.

questions.q: Glycolysis is also known as the
questions.explanation: EMP stands for Embden, Meyerhof and Parnas.

questions.q: Citric acid, the first product of the Krebs cycle, has how many carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Acetyl CoA (2C) joins oxaloacetic acid (4C) to give citric acid (6C).

questions.q: The part of ATP synthase that forms the channel through which protons cross the inner mitochondrial membrane is
questions.explanation: F0 is the channel; F1 is the headpiece that makes ATP.

questions.q: Fermentation is important to a cell without oxygen because it
options: regenerates NAD+ so that glycolysis can continue
questions.explanation: NADH is oxidised back to NAD+ when pyruvate is reduced.

questions.q: Yeast cells ferment 5 molecules of glucose. The net ATP produced is
questions.explanation: Fermentation yields a net of 2 ATP per glucose, so 5 x 2 = 10.

questions.q: Describe the link reaction between glycolysis and the Krebs cycle.
questions.answer: Pyruvic acid enters the mitochondrial matrix and undergoes oxidative decarboxylation with NAD+ and coenzyme A, catalysed by pyruvate dehydrogenase. It forms acetyl CoA, CO2 and NADH.
keyPoints: Pyruvate gives acetyl CoA and CO2
questions.explanation: Two acetyl CoA are formed per glucose.

questions.q: Why does oxidation of FADH2 yield fewer ATP molecules than that of NADH?
questions.answer: FADH2 passes its electrons into the chain at complex II, bypassing complex I, so fewer protons are pumped across the membrane and less ATP is produced (2 ATP against 3).
questions.explanation: ATP output depends on the proton gradient.

questions.q: The coiling of a pea tendril around a support is an example of
questions.explanation: Thigmotropism is a growth response to touch.

questions.q: Spraying grapes with gibberellin results in
questions.explanation: Gibberellins elongate the stalks and increase fruit size in grapes.

questions.q: Plants such as tomato that flower regardless of the length of day are called
questions.explanation: Day-neutral plants have no photoperiodic requirement.

questions.q: Which of these plant hormones is chiefly a growth inhibitor?
questions.explanation: ABA inhibits growth and promotes dormancy.

questions.q: Which hormone promotes the growth of lateral buds and so counteracts apical dominance?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins promote lateral bud growth, while auxin from the apex inhibits it.

questions.q: Short-day plants flower when
options: the light period is longer than a critical length
the dark period is longer than a critical length
questions.explanation: Flowering of short-day plants requires a dark period longer than a critical period.

questions.q: Define growth, differentiation and development in plants.
questions.answer: Growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size, mass or volume. Differentiation is the specialisation of cells for particular functions. Development covers all changes an organism goes through from seed germination to senescence.
keyPoints: Development: all changes in the life cycle
questions.explanation: Development includes both growth and differentiation.

questions.q: State four physiological roles of abscisic acid.
questions.answer: ABA closes stomata during water stress, induces seed dormancy, promotes abscission of leaves and fruits, and helps plants tolerate stresses such as drought; it also inhibits seed germination.
questions.explanation: ABA is known as the stress hormone.

questions.q: The hardest substance in the human body is
questions.explanation: Enamel covers the crown of the tooth.

questions.q: The lungs are located in the
questions.explanation: The lungs lie in the thoracic chamber, protected by the rib cage.

questions.q: The finger-like villi of the small intestine help to increase the
questions.explanation: Villi and microvilli greatly increase the absorptive surface.

questions.q: The first heart sound, 'lub', is due to the closure of the
questions.explanation: The second sound, 'dub', comes from the closure of the semilunar valves.

questions.q: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

questions.q: For a person whose heart beats 75 times a minute, the duration of one cardiac cycle is
questions.explanation: 60 s divided by 75 beats gives 0.8 s per cycle.

questions.q: Name, in order, the parts of the human alimentary canal through which food passes.
questions.answer: Mouth (buccal cavity), pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine (duodenum, jejunum, ileum), large intestine (caecum, colon, rectum) and anus.
questions.explanation: Digestive glands add secretions along the way.

questions.q: Why do people at high altitudes breathe faster at first?
questions.answer: The partial pressure of oxygen is lower at high altitude, so less oxygen reaches the blood; chemoreceptors detect this and increase the rate of breathing. In the long term the body makes more red blood cells.
questions.explanation: Faster breathing helps to supply enough oxygen.

questions.q: The outer region of the kidney is called the
questions.explanation: The cortex lies outside the medulla and contains the glomeruli.

questions.q: The only freely movable bone of the human skull is the
questions.explanation: The lower jaw bone, the mandible, moves at a joint with the temporal bone.

questions.q: The adrenal cortex hormone that regulates sodium and water balance is
questions.explanation: Aldosterone increases reabsorption of Na+ and water in the kidney tubules.

questions.q: The process of a neuron that carries impulses away from the cell body is the
questions.explanation: Axons transmit impulses to the synapse or the effector.

questions.q: Glomerular filtration is aided by the fact that the efferent arteriole is
questions.explanation: A narrower efferent vessel raises the blood pressure in the glomerular capillaries.

questions.q: Muscle fibres rich in myoglobin and mitochondria, which are suited to prolonged aerobic activity, are called
questions.explanation: Red fibres have plenty of myoglobin and use oxygen for sustained work.

questions.q: Differentiate between exocrine and endocrine glands with one example each.
questions.answer: Exocrine glands release their secretions through ducts, e.g. salivary glands; endocrine glands are ductless and secrete hormones directly into the blood, e.g. the thyroid.
questions.explanation: The pancreas has both exocrine and endocrine parts.

questions.q: Explain how negative feedback regulates ADH secretion.
questions.answer: When body fluids become more concentrated, osmoreceptors stimulate release of ADH, which increases water reabsorption, diluting the fluids. When fluid volume rises or the fluid is dilute, ADH release falls, so urine becomes more dilute and the balance is restored.
keyPoints: Restored balance switches off ADH release
questions.explanation: Feedback keeps body fluid concentration stable.
